Shows your **Guardian valve controller** (Elexa, GVC1) and the **leak
sensors** paired with it in Gladys through its **local API** (UDP port 7777):
no Guardian cloud, straight on your network.

> **Never tested with a real device.** Not affiliated with Elexa. The
> integration follows aioguardian, the Guardian library of Home Assistant,
> and the captures of its tests. A firmware update may change the API.

> **The local API has no password.** Anyone on your network can open or
> close the valve with it, with or without Gladys, and can forge its answers
> just as easily (the leak, the valve state, the UID: UDP without any
> authentication). The opening lock of Gladys and the confirmation "seen
> closed" are no safer than your network. Keep the controller on a trusted
> network (no guest Wi-Fi, no port forwarding).

## What you get

One device per controller and one per paired leak sensor, keyed by the UID
the device gives (never by its IP address):

| Device           | Feature               | Content                                                           |
| ---------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Valve controller | Valve                 | Text: open, closed, opening, closing, stalled, halted mid-way...  |
| Valve controller | Valve open            | 1 open, 0 closed (unchanged while it moves or is in a fault)      |
| Valve controller | Close the valve       | Button, **always available**                                      |
| Valve controller | Open the valve        | Button, only with "Allow opening the valve"                       |
| Valve controller | Leak (onboard sensor) | 1 leak, 0 dry                                                     |
| Valve controller | Temperature           | °C (the controller gives °F, converted exactly: (F - 32) x 5 / 9) |
| Leak sensor      | Leak, Temperature     | As above                                                          |
| Leak sensor      | Battery               | %                                                                 |
| Leak sensor      | Moved                 | 1 when the sensor reports it was moved                            |

Each controller is read every 30 seconds by default (10 s to 1 h), one
request at a time. The onboard sensor, the list of the paired sensors (every
10 minutes), each sensor and the diagnostics (firmware, every 6 hours) are
secondary: when one does not answer, the valve is published anyway and the
status says "Not read: ...". A value is never published as 0 when it is
unknown; a value read more than 2 minutes ago is never sent as new.

The controller keeps the last values of each sensor; the API gives no date
for them: a sensor whose battery is dead may keep showing its last values.

## Installation

1. Give the controller a fixed IP address in your router.
2. In Gladys, install the integration and enter the IP address of the
   controller (optionally followed by a port, 7777 by default). Several
   controllers: their addresses separated by commas (8 at most).
3. Save, then add the devices from the **Discovery** tab.

The controller is never searched on the network: no broadcast, no multicast.

## Closing the valve (always)

"Close the valve" is the stop of this integration: it is never held back by
an option, a read or an open in progress (it ends them), a controller that
did not answer the last read, the configuration not read yet, or a slow
disk. It goes:

- to the address where that valve answered since the start;
- else to the address where it was last read before a restart (kept in
  `/data`);
- else to every configured address whose controller was never identified
  (the address you typed).

It is sent at once. One try waits 1.2 s for the answer: after a silence it is
sent again at once, after a "moving" answer (the controller refuses any
command while its valve moves) 250 ms later, for 3 seconds. The first
"moving" answer reads the valve once: closing (a close already on its way,
from a check, a click just before or the button), the click is a close under
way, answered like an accepted one, never "refused"; closed, it is answered
"not confirmed yet", kept, and the next check (5 s later) confirms it (a
status read right after "moving" may lag behind an open starting). Then it is
**kept** in `/data` and checked every 15 seconds (5 seconds while the valve
closes), also after a restart, before Gladys even gives the configuration,
until a read shows the valve **closed**. It is sent again while the valve
stays open or in a fault: 3 times quickly (each accepted by the controller,
2.4 s apart); then, held, every 30 seconds, then less and less often (10
minutes apart at most), until the valve closes, and the status asks you to
check the valve. A valve that changes (out of its fault, moved by hand), a
controller that answers again after a silence or restarted (its uptime drops)
or a restart of the integration gives 3 quick resends again. A silence, an unreachable controller
or a "moving" answer never counts as a try.

When another valve (another UID) answers at the address the close went to
(addresses moved in the router), that other valve is closed too (the safe
side), and the close of the valve you clicked is **kept**: it goes where that
valve answers in this run, else to every configured address not identified
in this run; if there is none, it waits (in `/data`, said in the status)
until that valve answers at a configured address. The identity of every
configured address is read at once then (whatever the refresh interval), and
as soon as that valve answers at an address, every close of it kept for
another address goes there. Deleting that valve in Gladys gives up a close
still searched for. A close kept in `/data` whose UID cannot be read goes to
its address whatever valve answers there (the safe side).

The close is refused, nothing sent, in two cases only:

- no address is known at all (nothing configured, nothing in `/data`);
- every known address answers with another valve (another UID).

A close kept is let go only when: a read shows the valve closed; an open
clicked in Gladys (with the option) left before that close was clicked;
two reads in a row show the valve opened again after it was seen closing
(opened from the app or the button of the controller). Never by time; never
because another valve answers at its address (see above).

Gladys gets its answer within 3.5 seconds: success only when the read back
read the valve you clicked (its UID), closing or closed; otherwise the
message says exactly what happened (sent without an answer, not sent yet,
refused, moving, another valve at that address, identity not read yet), and
the close stays kept.

## Opening the valve (off by default)

"Allow opening the valve" is **off** by default: the button then refuses
every command. When it is on, an open is decided on a **fresh read** (never
on the values in memory) and refused when:

- the controller at the address is not the same one (UID), or cannot say;
- the valve moves, or is in a fault (stalled, motor spinning, halted, position
  unknown);
- the onboard sensor reads a leak, or cannot be read;
- a paired sensor reads a leak, or cannot be read in time (each one listed
  is read; a sensor whose battery is dead blocks opening: remove it in the
  Guardian app), or the list of the paired sensors cannot be read;
- a close of that controller is being sent (a close clicked after an open
  always wins: the open never leaves after it, and an open that already left
  never lets that close go);
- the option is turned off before the datagram leaves;
- a close is kept for that valve and `/data` cannot be written (a restart
  would close it again);
- `/data` is still being read (a close kept there could come back and close
  the valve again);
- the controller does not answer in time (nothing sent after 2.7 s).

An open is confirmed only by a read back showing the valve opening or open;
otherwise "sent, without confirmation", and the valve is read again after 5
and 20 seconds. The integration never halts the valve (a halted Guardian no
longer reacts to its leak sensors).

## Status

The configuration screen shows, for each controller: its UID, the valve,
the number of paired sensors, a leak, the parts not read, and for each close
kept where it stands. "Test the connection" reads each controller once,
never sooner than the refresh interval.

## Limits

- Tested only against a fake controller built from aioguardian 2026.1.1 and
  its fixtures; never with a real device.
- No firmware update, Wi-Fi setup, pairing, reboot or factory reset from
  Gladys: use the Guardian app.
- The API has no authentication (see above).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Guardian (Elexa) asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Guardian valve controller | `section` | No | Shows your Guardian valve controller (Elexa, GVC1) and the leak sensors paired with it in Gladys through its local API, without the Guardian cloud: valve state, leaks, temperatures, sensor batteries. Closing the valve always works from Gladys; opening it only if you allow it below. The local API has no password: anyone on your network can command the valve and forge its answers, keep it on a trusted network. Give the controller a fixed address in your router, enter it, save, then add the devices from the Discovery tab. Never tested with a real device. Not affiliated with Elexa. |
| IP address of the controller | `string` | Yes | An IPv4 address or a host name, optionally followed by a port (7777 by default). Several controllers: their addresses separated by commas (8 at most). Never a broadcast or multicast address: the controller is not searched on the network. |
| Allow opening the valve | `boolean` | No | Off by default. On: the "Open the valve" button lets water in, after a fresh read shows the valve still (closed; or open while a close is kept, which the open then lets go), no leak on the controller nor on any paired sensor (each one read). Off: it refuses every command. Closing the valve always works. |
| Refresh interval (seconds) | `number` | No | How often each controller is read, 10 to 3600 seconds (30 by default). |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | The language of the names given to the devices and their features. |

## How to install Guardian (Elexa) in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Guardian (Elexa) appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-guardian:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-guardian](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-guardian).

Guardian (Elexa) requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Guardian (Elexa) is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
